sources.title: Mitsui Fudosan, Kumagai Gumi and Getworks announce Kobe host-tunnel data center
sources.summary: Named development uses the awarded 3-km section of the municipal former conveyor tunnel. First service is targeted for end-2027; eventual maximum 20 MW receiving capacity is a plan, not live IT power. Roles table identifies Mitsui and Kumagai as site developers, Getworks as container-DC operator, and Kumagai as intended works contractor.
sources.date_semantics: October 6 announcement supports announced lifecycle. September 4 is lease-award decision. Existing historical tunnel and development-start language do not prove physical DC construction.

sources.title: Kobe city announces conveyor-tunnel lease award and identifies the selected section
sources.summary: City identifies the Komi-to-Mitsugaoka section in Nishi Ward, approximately 3 km and 17000 square metres, with Mitsui Fudosan as lead and Kumagai Gumi as consortium member. City links its location map and the developer announcement.
sources.date_semantics: October 6 press release reports September 4 bid opening/award. No achieved construction date stated.

sources.title: Official lease map: D4 machine room, D4 tunnel and D3 machine room corridor
sources.summary: One-page lease map explicitly highlights D4 machine room through D4 tunnel to D3 machine room and a short D3 section. Its D4 symbol has been registered to official GSI map tiles and selected only as an approximate host-facility marker.
sources.date_semantics: Undated attachment linked by October 6 award release. PDF metadata June 2026 is not claimed as publication date; used for geometry only.

sources.title: GSI standard tile specification
sources.summary: Defines 256-pixel XYZ map tiles in Web Mercator; numeric tile addresses anchor the georeference to longitude and latitude.
sources.date_semantics: Undated technical reference, retrieved October 13. Geometry reference only.

sources.title: GSI standard map tiles supporting Kobe D4 host-tunnel georeference
sources.attribution: Geospatial Information Authority of Japan (GSI) standard map tiles; analyst-derived georeference
sources.summary: Official standard map tile containing the selected D4 marker. Geometry facts list all used control-point tile hashes and URLs. Nineteen spatially distributed tie points register the municipal diagram; residual does not measure total ground accuracy.
sources.date_semantics: Tile retrieval date is not map-observation or physical project-status date.

sources.title: Miyagi AI Data Center completed July 24
sources.summary: Named container facility on unused Tohoku Electric land in Shichigahama completed July 24. July 31 service launch is prospective in this release. Exact property identity remains undisclosed in the release.
sources.date_semantics: Explicit same-day completion; planned service date is not an achieved date.

sources.title: OCX network node opened September 1 at Miyagi AI Data Center
sources.summary: Named Miyagi AI DC OCX node opened September 1. Supports achieved network service at the host; gives only Shichigahama municipality and cannot resolve a physical map point.
sources.date_semantics: September 30 publication reports September 1 achieved network-node opening. Not proof every GPU container is commissioned.

sources.title: OCX physical connection site list
sources.summary: Lists Miyagi AI Data Center as JP-East-0034 in Shichigahama, Miyagi; location remains municipality-level.
sources.date_semantics: Undated site list retrieved October 13; not a new physical status observation.
